_scope: Hyperspace is not ported yet, so the denominator is the shared C++ core plus
the Hyperspace files the port has taken off GL: code that runs without a GL
context. Some of it still compiles against GL headers for types (below).
Deliberately outside it, and why:
Hyperspace/*.cpp   the simulation still calls OpenGL directly -- except
transform.cpp, renderer.cpp, stretchedParticle.cpp and
flare.cpp, which the port has taken out of GL, and
splinePath.cpp, which never called GL and is not in
yet (ss-65n)
rsText/rsText.cpp  builds display lists; GL-coupled
HyperspaceView.mm  AppKit/NSOpenGLView; needs a host process
As the port replaces those with testable code, move them into sources --
the ratchet will hold whatever coverage they arrive with.
Note the include style: this repo uses <rsMath/rsMath.h>, so the repo root
is on the include path rather than each source directory.
OpenGL is linked because this repo's Implicit/impSurface.cpp still calls it
from draw() and the destructor. Helios carries the same GL-coupled copy --
it had de-GL'd it during its Metal port, but that fork was deleted and
re-forked back to a pre-port state, so the two agree again. Drop the
framework once hyperspace is ported, or once the shared core is extracted
and unified. The GL headers stay needed longer than the framework: the
Hyperspace sources here include Hyperspace.h, whose settings struct still
declares GLuint and GLint fields.
Denominator change, 2026-08-22 (ss-3c8). The line count fell 2394 -> 2388 and
the baseline rose 83.79% -> 84.00% WITHOUT any test being written. Recorded
here because INV1 makes a shrinking denominator a decision that has to be
argued for, not a number that is allowed to improve quietly.
Note what did NOT change: 'covered' stayed at 2006. Six uncovered lines left
the denominator and no covered line was added, which is exactly the shape
removing dead code should have. (An earlier draft of this note said 2393 ->
2388, taken from the committed baseline's 'covered'/'count' fields. Those are
write-only and go stale whenever a change moves coverage by <= 0.01 points --
ss-8hh. Measure instead, and mind the argument: the working invocation is
'tools/coverage.sh --json <dir> hyperspace', which writes the report to
<dir>/hyperspace.json. Bare '--json' dies on an unbound $2, and '--json hyperspace'
reads hyperspace as the output DIRECTORY and silently measures all three
submodules -- that is ss-hye.)
What changed: impSurface::addTriStripLength was guarded '#ifdef
USE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS' at its declaration and definition while every call site
used '#if'. The macro is #defined as 0, so #ifdef was true and #if was false --
the function compiled into the binary with no caller anywhere, and llvm-cov
counted its regions as permanently uncoverable. Both guards are now '#if', so
it is not compiled at all.
Why this is the code improving rather than the measurement moving: nothing was
excluded, no source was removed from 'sources', and the function is still
compiled -- and still measured -- if anyone sets USE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS to 1,
which was verified to compile before and after the change. What left the
denominator is dead code, which is the one direction INV1 permits.
The 84.00% above is what the baseline read on the day, and it is deliberately
not updated: this entry records what ss-3c8 did, not where the number stands.
It has since moved to 96.52% for an unrelated reason -- ss-c49 and ss-qsv,
which added tests rather than touching scope. The denominator stayed 2388
until 2026-11-15, when transform.cpp joined (see the entry below).
Scope grows, 2026-11-15 (ss-a4a.4.1, hyperspace#22). Hyperspace/transform.cpp
joins sources: the camera, billboard and projection maths used to run on the GL
matrix stack and GLU, and now runs as plain functions that need no context. It is
the first file the Metal port has taken out of GL, and it arrives at 100% (75/75).
Measured: count 2388 -> 2463 and covered 2305 -> 2380, both +75 -- exactly this
file, so the baseline moved 96.52% -> 96.63% because tested code was added, not
because anything left the denominator. (A first draft of this PR carried a baseline
written against an earlier revision of the file, 2461/2378; it was regenerated with
--update-baseline against the pinned commit rather than edited.)
The submodule's tests workflow mirrors this list by hand and lists the file too;
tools/tests/test_ci_source_lists.py now fails when the two disagree.
Scope grows, 2026-11-15 (ss-a4a.4.1). The stars and the lens flare draw through
HSRenderer (Hyperspace/renderer.h) and compute their own vertices, so
Hyperspace/renderer.cpp, stretchedParticle.cpp and flare.cpp make no GL calls
and join sources. They still include GL headers, for the GLuint/GLint fields
of the settings struct in Hyperspace.h; the Metal port retypes those. The GL backend, rendererGL.cpp, stays out: it is the GL.
Measured: count 2463 -> 2724 (+261) and covered 2380 -> 2636 (+256). That is
exactly these files plus transform.cpp's new hsApply: renderer 8/8,
stretchedParticle 62/62, flare 182/187, transform +4/+4. Nothing left the
denominator. The ratchet raised the baseline 96.63% -> 96.77% on its own.
flare.cpp's 5 uncovered lines are clamps in the flare texture generation that
no pixel reaches (temp is already within 0..1 there).
